To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified the CHZ-O-Glucuronide (a major metabolite) and a new metabolite, the N-Glucuronides of CHZ (CHZ-N-glucuronic acid) produced in vitro and in human liver slices and in vivo (mouse and human urine).

(i) the CHZ-O-Glucuronide is a new metabolite detected in culture media of hepatocytes, liver slices and in urine of mice and humans; (ii) the CHZ-N- Glucuronide is also a new metabolite produced in hepatocytes independently of the Cyp2E1 activity; (iii) the CHZ- O- Glucuronides are synthesized by UGT1 family members; (iv) the Cyp2e1-dependent
we identified a novel metabolite produced from chlorzoxazones and its glucuronide, which is resistant to hydrolysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolism of the CHZ in vitro and in mice and humans and the identification of the UGT isoforms involved in the glucuronidation.
the identification of new metabolites of CH Z, the determination of their metabolic pathways and the identification of the UGTs involved in their production.
the development of new methods for assessing CYP2E activity and UGT activity in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the OH-CH Z glucuronide is the most reliable biomarker of CYP2E 1 activity in vitro and in humans.
CYP2E activity can be assessed by quantifying the hydroxylated metabolite (OH-CH) after enzymatic hydrolyzation of the glucuronides.

CHZ-O-Glu and CHZ-N-Glu are the two major metabolites of CHz in humans and that the measurement of the OH- CHZ in urine following enzymatic hydroxylation of CHZ glucoronides is the most reliable assay for the quantification of CYP2E activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CHZ-O-Glu is produced by CYP2e1 dependent pathway and CHZ-O-Gluc is produced by Cyp2e1 independent pathway.
CYP2E is responsible for CHZ hydroxyzation, and UGT1A is responsible for CHz glucuronidation, however, CHZ-O-glucuoride and CHZ-N-glucuoride are both produced.
CHZ is metabolized via two pathways in humans, one dependent and the other independent of CYP2E activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quantification of OH-CHz in human liver slices or in vivo is not sufficient to measure CYP2E activity because of the production of CHZ-O-gluronide.
CHZ is metabolized by CYP2Es and UGTs in vitro and in humans.
CHZ is a substrate for both UGT1A and UGT2B enzymes.
